1.title: Chat Client with the Foundry SDK
1.text: Welcome to Module eight: Chat Client with the Foundry S D K. It covers the exam area Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. The idea. Install and sign in. The program. Common mistakes. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (fifty-five to sixty percent). Exam format: a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes; check the exam page for the time. Validated against: the official A I nine oh one study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: The idea
1.text: The idea. A chat client application is a small program that sends a prompt to a deployed model and prints the reply. The Foundry S D K gives you the Python (and C, Java Script, Java) building blocks. The exam wants you to read a short program and say what each part does.

1.title: The idea, continued
1.text: The idea. one. Sign in. Uses your Microsoft Entra I D identity through Default Azure Credential. two. Connect. Creates a project client with the project endpoint. three. Get a model client. Asks the project client for an Open A I-compatible client. four. Send the prompt. Calls the model by its deployment name with your input. five. Read the reply. Prints the output text.

1.title: The idea, continued
1.text: The idea. The figure shows this: Five steps of a chat client: sign in, connect, get client, send, read.

1.title: Install and sign in
1.text: Install and sign in. Install the S D K with pip install azure ai projects two dot three dot zero. The sample uses Default Azure Credential, which comes from the azure-identity package. Azure A I Projects two.x is not compatible with one.x: sample code for the older version looks different. Sign in first with the Azure C L I command A Z login; Default Azure Credential then picks up your sign-in. No key is written into the code. Exam tip: "No secret in the source code" to Default Azure Credential with Microsoft Entra I D. The identity needs permission on the project. Exam tip: No secret in the source code: Default Azure Credential uses your Microsoft Entra I D sign-in (after A Z login ).

1.title: The program
1.text: The program. This is the short program from the Microsoft quickstart. Read it line by line. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: The program, continued
1.text: The program. A I Project Client endpoint..., credential... Connects to the Foundry project with your identity. project dot get openai client. Returns an Open A I-compatible client for models in the project. openai dot responses dot create... Sends the request using the Responses A P I. model G P T five mini. The deployment name of the model you deployed. input... The user prompt. response dot output text. The text of the reply. The endpoint looks like H T T P S colon slash slash resource name dot services dot ai dot azure dot com slash api slash projects slash project name. The model value must match a deployment in the project. A wrong name gives an error that the deployment was not found.

1.title: The program, continued
1.text: The program. To set the assistant's behavior you add instructions (a system prompt). for the exact parameter. For a multi-turn chat, the app keeps the earlier messages and sends them again (Module two). Check the sample code for the exact input format. Exam tip: Identify the parts: client creation (endpoint plus credential), model call (deployment name plus input), output ( output text ). A question may ask what to change to use another model (change the deployment name) or another project (change the endpoint).

1.title: Common mistakes
1.text: Common mistakes. Authentication error. Not signed in ( A Z login ) or no permission on the project. "Deployment not found". The model value does not match a deployment name. Reply cut off. Max output tokens too low. Works in the playground, fails in code. Wrong endpoint or a different project. Sample code from an old tutorial fails. S D K version one.x code with a two.x package.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A Fabrikam Outdoors developer wants Python code to authenticate without storing a key in the source file. What should the code use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Default Azure Credential with the signed-in identity. Default Azure Credential uses Microsoft Entra I D sign-in, so no secret is stored in the code.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. In the sample program, what does A I Project Client endpoint..., credential... do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Connects the program to the Foundry project. It creates the client that connects to the project through its endpoint.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A call fails because the deployment cannot be found. What should the developer check? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: That the model value matches the deployment name in the project. The model parameter must be the name of a deployment in the project.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which property of the response object holds the text answer in the sample? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: response.output text. The sample prints response dot output text.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. The team deploys a second model named chat small and wants the program to use it. What is the smallest change? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Change the model value to chat small. The model value is the deployment name, so changing it selects another deployment.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which command signs in so that Default Azure Credential can find your identity during development? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A Z login. The quickstart says to sign in with the Azure C L I A Z login command first.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which Python package provides the Foundry project client? Answer: azure A I projects. Question two. Which class connects to a project? Answer: A I Project Client. Question three. Which method returns an Open A I-compatible client? Answer: get openai client.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which value in the call is the deployment name? Answer: The model argument. Question five. Where is the answer text in the response? Answer: output text. Question six. Which authentication class avoids storing a key in code? Answer: Default Azure Credential.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Steps: sign in, connect, get client, send the prompt, read the reply. Packages: azure A I projects (two.x) and azure-identity. Connect: A I Project Client(endpoint, credential equals Default Azure Credential()). Call: project.get openai client(); openai.responses.create(model equals deployment, input equals prompt). Read: response.output text. Troubleshoot: A Z login, permission, deployment name, endpoint, token limit. In the next module, we continue the course.
